title: Stage 3: The model
summary: Build a star schema: customer and book dimensions around a sales fact table.

steps.title: A star schema
body: Staging is clean but still one wide table, with names and titles repeated on every line. For analysis, warehouses use a **star schema**:
- **Fact table**: one row per event you measure (an order line), holding **keys** and **numbers** (`qty`, `revenue_cents`).
- **Dimension tables**: one row per thing you slice by (a customer, a book), holding descriptive text.

It's normalisation (module 7) applied with a purpose: facts stay narrow and fast to aggregate, and a customer's name lives in exactly one place. Dimensions get their own **surrogate keys** (`customer_id`), so the model doesn't break if an email changes.

items: which book and customer an order line refers to (as keys)

steps.title: Load the dimensions
prompt: Create and fill the two dimension tables from `stg_orders`:
- **`dim_customer(customer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, name TEXT NOT NULL)`**: one row per customer email
- **`dim_book(book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, isbn TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, title TEXT NOT NULL)`**: one row per ISBN
Tables: `stg_orders(order_ref, order_date, email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_cents, channel)` (13 cleaned rows).
solution: CREATE TABLE dim_customer (customer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, name TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE dim_book (book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, isbn TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, title TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO dim_customer (email, name) SELECT DISTINCT email, customer_name FROM stg_orders;
INSERT INTO dim_book (isbn, title) SELECT DISTINCT isbn, title FROM stg_orders;

steps.title: Load the fact table
prompt: Primary key (`order_ref`, `book_id`). Fill it from `stg_orders`, looking up the surrogate keys by email and ISBN; `revenue_cents` is `qty * unit_cents`.
Tables: `stg_orders(order_ref, order_date, email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_cents, channel)`, `dim_customer(customer_id, email, name)`, `dim_book(book_id, isbn, title)`.
solution: customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_customer(customer_id),
book_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_book(book_id),
SELECT s.order_ref, s.order_date, c.customer_id, b.book_id, s.channel, s.qty, s.qty * s.unit_cents
JOIN dim_customer AS c ON c.email = s.email
JOIN dim_book AS b ON b.isbn = s.isbn;
setup: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
CREATE TABLE raw_orders (order_ref TEXT, order_date TEXT, customer_email TEXT, customer_name TEXT, isbn TEXT, title TEXT, qty TEXT, unit_price TEXT, channel TEXT);
